text:
maria: Quick sync — designing AWS KMS integration for Redwood Private (customer VPC / BYOK). Questions: control-plane keys vs data-plane keys, how we want grants vs IAM, and audit expectations. Anyone mapped this end-to-end?
aj: I sketched two-mode approach: 1) control-plane CMK (optionally in customer account for BYOK) used to encrypt control-plane secrets and DEKs metadata; 2) data-plane CMKs to wrap per-tenant DEKs for payloads. Keep them separate for blast radius.
jenna: agree. Important: control-plane SHOULD be able to use a customer CMK (BYOK) when they choose private deployment. We need clear docs on the required key policy and the IAM role we assume.
sam: +1. Also remember VPC endpoints: when calling KMS from inside private VPC, we need to require kms:ViaService condition on the key policy to limit usage to the VPC endpoint/service.
aj: example key policy snippet I used in test (paste):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodControlPlane",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDCUSTOMERACCOUNT:role/RedwoodControlPlaneRole"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*",
      "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"kms:ViaService": "kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com"}}
    }
  ]
}
```
maria: That policy is fine as an example, but we should recommend customers add `kms:CallerAccount` or limit principals by account ID. Also for cross-account BYOK we need to call out Grant vs KeyPolicy tradeoffs.
jenna: On grants: prefer short-lived grants for the runtime servers that need Encrypt/Decrypt to avoid changing key policy frequently. Use `CreateGrant` + cached grant tokens. It also avoids cross-account policy churn.
sam: For rotation plan — we should define SLO: key rotation must not cause decryption failures. Plan: 1) create new CMK, 2) start writing new DEKs encrypted under new CMK, 3) run background rewrap jobs to re-encrypt older DEKs, 4) after all DEKs rewrapped and no references to old key exist, schedule schedule disable -> schedule deletion window.
aj: rewrap job steps: scan metadata table for DEK versions -> call KMS `ReEncrypt` from old CMK to new CMK -> update metadata to point to new wrapped DEK. Use batching and backoff to avoid throttling.
jenna: Audit/logging: enable CloudTrail KMS data events and alert on `ReEncrypt`/`DisableKey`/`RetireGrant`/`CreateGrant` calls. Ship logs to SIEM and correlate with our control-plane principal.
kms-bot: Tip: also include AWS Config rule `kms-key-rotation-enabled` or custom rule to ensure CMKs configured as expected. If using AWS-managed keys, note rotation semantics differ vs customer-managed CMKs.
maria: operational notes: - Recommend rotation cadence: control-plane CMK annually, data-plane CMKs can be longer if rewrap overhead is huge. - Keep old CMK for decrypt-only until rewrap complete. - Provide a 'dry-run' rewrap utility in the console SDK so customers can estimate time/cost.
aj: Terraform snippet we used in POC (sanitized):
```
resource "aws_kms_key" "control_plane" {
  description             = "Redwood Private control-plane CMK (BYOK friendly)"
  deletion_window_in_days = 30
  enable_key_rotation     = true
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "redwood_control_plane" {
  name = "RedwoodControlPlaneRole"
  # assume role trust policy to allow our control plane account
}
```
sam: Edge cases: - VPC endpoints + KMS via service across accounts can be tricky; test with interface endpoint and confirm kms:ViaService value. - For offline/air-gapped on-prem customers we need to support customer HSM imports or a local envelope key mechanism.
jenna: Next action items: (1) write a short runbook for BYOK key policy + minimal IAM role + grant pattern; (2) add CloudTrail alert playbook; (3) prototype rewrap utility in dev env and document costs.
maria: I'll draft the runbook. tagging @aj and @sam for review. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
